source.title: Scaling Down Deep Learning with MNIST-1D

record.tranche_reason: Directly sweeps model size and measures test error around the training interpolation threshold, applying the model-wise double-descent test on the new MNIST-1D benchmark.
record.gate_note: The study's own size-sweep results are in Figure 5. Its general description of epoch-wise and data-wise double descent is background, not a reported test of those versions. Figure 9 varies sample counts for a pooling comparison, but does not test whether more data raises test error near an interpolation threshold. Cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 5.2 and Figure 5 sweep MLP hidden-layer width and CNN channel count on MNIST-1D, with and without 15% label noise. They report test and train error around the interpolation threshold, the same method and measure as Nakkiran et al. on a new dataset.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also frame the result mainly as showing that MNIST-1D is a cheap testbed for studying double descent, rather than as a new finding about it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a different, procedurally generated dataset (MNIST-1D), with an MLP hidden-layer-width sweep and a three-convolutional-layer CNN channel sweep; the figure is adapted from Prince (2023).
record.method_sensitivity: For the MLP, the peak differs between the 15% label-noise and no-label-noise conditions.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The double-descent evidence is reported qualitatively from Figure 5, with no uncertainty estimates stated for those results. It is tested on MNIST-1D only.

untested.parts: Only MNIST-1D, a single-hidden-layer MLP and a three-layer CNN. No other datasets or architectures, and no uncertainty over runs.
Not tested: no epoch-wise sweep of test error. Mentioned only as background.
Not tested. The Figure 9 sample-size variation is a pooling comparison, not near-interpolation test error.
Only the presence or absence of label noise is tested. Not tested: variance as a cause, multiple peaks, regularization, and the CNN without noise.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 5 is adapted from Prince (2023, Section 8.4), and Prince helped improve the experiments. The authors still present it as their own observation, so it is kept as study results. All evidence is figure-only and qualitative, with no error bars. Tranche could arguably be T3, since the dataset is new while the method matches the original.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests model-size sweeps on MNIST-1D, not the claim across other datasets or settings.
No test-error double-descent sweep over training epochs is reported.
The study does not test whether increasing sample size near interpolation raises test error.
The reported tests use MLP and CNN neural networks; they do not test a general curve across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
The study compares label-noise and no-label-noise conditions, but does not test variance as a cause, multiple or triple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters.

statements.problem: The text establishes no clean-label test-error peak, but does not explicitly establish monotonicity; the extracted figure does not resolve that stronger description.
